subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: CRISPR: Engineering Life Itself
description: A fast breakdown of CRISPR: Engineering Life Itself for builders.

hook.text: In 2018, a scientist edited two human embryos to resist HIV. The world was horrified.

buildup.text: CRISPR-Cas9 lets scientists cut DNA at exact locations, like a molecular word processor.

discovery.text: Bacteria invented the system. They store virus DNA as a mugshot, then cut it if the virus returns.

twist.text: Jennifer Doudna, who helped discover it, has nightmares about its misuse. She won the Nobel anyway.

climax.text: CRISPR could eliminate genetic diseases, engineer crops, or create designer babies. The line is unclear.

punchline.text: We can edit life. The question is: should we?

quiz.question: Where did the CRISPR gene-editing system originally come from?
options: It was designed from scratch in a university lab
Bacteria use it to recognize and cut invading virus DNA
It was discovered inside cancer cells during treatment
